headline: The day America heard two noons

scenes.text: [calmly] On this day, in eighteen eighty-three... many American towns had noon twice.

scenes.label: Standard railway time
scenes.caption: Time zone map, 1880s
scenes.text: [thoughtfully] Before then, towns set clocks by the sun... over three hundred local times.

scenes.label: time zones for the United States
scenes.text: [calmly] Then railroads created four time zones, and reset station clocks at standard noon.

scenes.label: Chicago, Illinois
scenes.caption: Plaque marking the time system
scenes.text: [softly] It was the railroads' plan, not the government's.

scenes.title: Law only in 1918
scenes.text: [thoughtfully] Congress made it law only in nineteen eighteen.

scenes.title: Could you keep up with that?
scenes.text: [gently] Could you keep up with that?
